clues: This city lies in a valley among the Himalayas. It stands by the Jhelum River, on the shores of Dal Lake and one more lake.
High peaks ring this valley and block the wet winds from the south. So spring is its wettest time, while fall stays the driest of all.
This city was founded in the sixth century, in the days of the Gonanda kings. Their tale is told in an old book of the valley's past.
Houseboats line the shores of Dal Lake, each one a home that floats on the water. They are one of the sights this city is best known for.
Two famed gardens from Mughal days grace the shores of its great lake. Shalimar and Nishat are the pair that guests seek out most.
